"Well, that's a new one…don't know who Tall Dark and Trigger-Happy is, but he looks to have a grudge against you, Squid-Head, and just your luck that he turns up right now.  Sure is funny how this beauty works, but it always gets the job done."  Kismet holds up her "beauty" for a moment and inspects it, before tucking it away again and resuming her attack on Helena.  By now, Haka at least has sense enough to realize that the growing pain in his head is caused by more than the girl's relentlessly ascerbic repartee; apparently the artifact she wields is warping reality in subtle ways, some of which are in the process of giving him - and likely the other two heroes - the beginnings of a cerebral hemorrhage.  Attempting to stop this outrage against Nature, Haka raises his taiaha and charges - and trips, the weapon swinging wild as he falls and smashing into a component of the technological armature which Tempest wears (which he knows to be an Elemental Subwave Inducter, though he's never explained this to the Maori warrior, figuring he likely wouldn't especially care what it was called, only that it's largely responsible for the Maerynian's weather-control powers).  The ruptured power cell explodes with a faint "pop", and Tempest can smell the sizzling of his own flesh from a mild plasma burn. posts.cooked: Obstruction only checks once per turn.  This time, Rift in Time is discarded.  (I have something of a problem with the fact that the bottoming-unwanted-draws rule renders the environment deck predictable in fairly short order, and thus deprives cards like Inconceivable of a lot of their surprise value.  There are only three unknown enviro cards left, so if Haka damages Kismet, there's a 1/3 chance of IO intercepting the damage, and if it does not, Tempest faces a 1/2 chance, and after that the entire enviro deck will be known so there are no surprises left from the card.  For the moment I'll just roll with it, but I might end up changing the original SCUverse rules to make these situations more interesting.)
